title: 『2024-2025 年末年始台湾 ８日間⑧　～５日目午前：台北観光　故宮博物院訪問と絶品魯肉飯と豚足を食す～』台北(台湾)の旅行記・ブログ by たびっこさんciteフォートラベル
description:
National Palace Museum Entrance

A family trip to Taipei’s National Palace Museum begins with a quiet morning arrival at the grand marble staircases leading up to the main hall. Taiwanese flags line the white balustrades, and the museum’s green-tiled roofs and pale yellow walls stand out against a backdrop of wooded hills under a cloudy sky. Only a handful of visitors are present before opening, allowing for unobstructed photos of the iconic facade.

Inside, the group uses their Taipei FunPASS to bypass the regular ticket line and store their luggage in self-service lockers. They explore renowned exhibits such as the Jadeite Cabbage and Mao Gong Ding, noting that some treasures like the Meat-Shaped Stone are on loan elsewhere. After a thorough tour of the first-floor galleries, they plan to continue their cultural and culinary adventure in Taipei, sampling local specialties and visiting other landmarks throughout the day.

title: The Taiwan of Hou Hsiao-Hsien and Edward Yang – Taiwan Scene
description:
Jiufen’s Iconic Tea House

Nestled on a ridge overlooking Taiwan’s northeast coast, this multi‑story tea house in Jiufen is clad in dark wood and festooned with red lanterns and Chinese banners reading “阿妹茶樓.” The narrow stairways and balconies bustle with visitors, while potted greenery softens the traditional architecture. 

Famous as a filming location for Hou Hsiao‑Hsien’s A City of Sadness, the tea house retains its historic charm. Open windows reveal cozy interior seating, and the surrounding misty hills hint at the town’s former mining heritage and timeless allure.

title: 淡水老街 景點- (VRbyby 全國廟宇網)
description:
Tamsui Riverside Promenade

A tranquil riverside walkway in Tamsui Old Street features colorful wooden boats gently bobbing on the water beside a stone-paved path. Trees line the promenade, providing shade for visitors who wander past small shops and food stalls. A red circular sign bearing the character “停” stands near a bench where a visitor sits, adding a touch of local signage to the scene.

Tamsui Old Street, once called Huwei, stretches along Zhongzheng Road beside the MRT Tamsui Station plaza and follows the Tamsui River’s edge. Known for its historic architecture and famous local snacks—iron eggs, shrimp rolls, A-gei, fish crisps, and grilled squid—the area welcomes tourists year-round. The calm water, overcast sky, and leisurely pace of pedestrians capture the laid-back charm of this northern Taiwan landmark.

title: 大稻埕實景導覽照片
description:
Red Brick Arcade and Parked Scooters

A two‑story red brick arcade building stands along Dihua Street in Taipei’s Datong District, showcasing a row of elegant arches on the ground floor and large, multi‑pane windows above. The façade features decorative stone panels and traditional Chinese characters reading “豐濱,” hinting at the building’s historical or commercial significance. 

In front of the arcade, a neat line of motor scooters occupies the street parking spaces, reflecting the daily rhythm of urban commuters. The contrast between the vintage brick architecture and the modern scooters captures the blend of heritage and contemporary life in Taipei. The bright daylight illuminates the scene, emphasizing the textures of the brickwork and the vibrant colors of the parked vehicles.

title: Fate of 'Queen's Head' uncertain despite efforts to save it - Focus Taiwan
description:
Queen’s Head at Yehliu Geopark

The Queen’s Head, a honey‑colored sandstone formation, stands on a flat coastal shelf in northern Taiwan. Its narrow neck supports a larger, weather‑eroded head, marked by pockmarks and wind‑sculpted textures. Warm afternoon light accentuates the rock’s golden hues and the smooth, undulating surface of the surrounding platform.

Authorities have implemented reinforcement measures to protect the Queen’s Head from further thinning and potential collapse. Despite these efforts, ongoing natural erosion and visitor impact continue to pose risks to this emblematic landmark.

title: 日月潭拉魯島 > 南投縣 > 交通部觀光署
description:
Lalu Island at Sun Moon Lake

An aerial photograph showcases Lalu Island, a small circular islet at the heart of Sun Moon Lake in Nantou County, Taiwan. The island’s lush green center and sandy perimeter are surrounded by a ring of floating platforms, with several boats docked nearby. The lake’s clear turquoise waters reflect the sky, enhancing the tranquil mood of the scene.

Lalu Island, known locally as the “floating islet,” divides Sun Moon Lake into two distinct halves—one resembling a sun and the other a crescent moon. This unique formation and the island’s central position make it one of the most celebrated scenic spots in Taiwan.

title: 景觀相簿(第2頁列表) - 清境民宿_雲濛仙境民宿
description:
Pastoral Scene at Cingjing Farm

A flock of woolly sheep peacefully grazes on a verdant hillside, their creamy coats standing out against the bright green grass. Beyond the meadow, a dense line of trees gives way to a cluster of houses perched on rolling hills, while misty mountains stretch into the distance under a soft, overcast sky.

This photograph captures the tranquil beauty of Cingjing Farm in Taiwan, known for its highland pastures and scenic vistas. The layered landscape—from the grazing sheep to the distant mountain peaks—highlights the region’s serene, rural charm.

title: Gaomei Wetland－Taichung Tourism
description:
Sunset Stroll on Gaomei Wetland Boardwalk

A gently curving wooden boardwalk winds across the expansive mudflats of Gaomei Wetland, bathed in the warm glow of a setting sun. Visitors pause along the path, taking in the serene vista where shallow pools mirror the sky’s golden hues and distant wind turbines stand sentinel along the horizon.

Gaomei Wetland spans 1,500 acres south of the Dajia River mouth, featuring a mix of sand and soil that supports Taiwan’s largest stand of Bolboschoenus planiculmis. Each fall and winter, migrating birds flock here, drawn by the diverse habitats. The reserve offers amenities such as a service center, parking, restrooms, viewing platforms, trails, and a bus stop, making it an accessible and popular spot for nature enthusiasts and bird-watchers alike.

title: 『全７都市巡る台湾縦断』台北(台湾)の旅行記・ブログ by edih7さんciteフォートラベル
description:
Taichung’s Rainbow Village

A group of visitors strolls along a narrow lane in Taichung’s Rainbow Village, marveling at the riot of color that envelops every surface. The humble row of single-story houses has been transformed into a vibrant open-air gallery by an elderly local artist, whose whimsical designs feature flowers, animals, and smiling faces in bold primary hues. Under a bright midday sun, the painted walls and ground patterns create a cheerful, immersive environment that draws photographers and art lovers alike.

This stop was part of a larger seven-city Taiwan tour, which included Taipei’s iconic 101 observatory, the lantern-lit sky of Shifen, and the nostalgic alleys of Jiufen. Travelers rated the overall experience highly for sightseeing and transportation, noting the ease of bus and high-speed rail connections. The Rainbow Village stands out as a testament to individual creativity, turning a once-forgotten military settlement into one of central Taiwan’s most Instagrammed landmarks.

title: 摸乳巷-遊憩景點-彰化旅遊資訊網
description:
Mōrǔ Xiàng (Breast-Touching Lane)

Nestled in Lukang, Changhua County, this historic alley measures under 70 centimeters at its narrowest point, forcing passersby to brush shoulders as they traverse the red-brick corridor. A faded red doorframe at the entrance displays vertical couplets reading “摸乳巷裡無乳摸,” hinting at the alley’s cheeky moniker. Overhead, verdant foliage softens the brick walls, while a lone visitor stands at the far end, illustrating the alley’s intimate scale.

Originally designed as a firebreak between long row houses and to shield interiors from strong sea winds, the passage earned various names—“Chest-Guarding Lane” and “Gentlemen’s Lane”—before the blunt “Breast-Touching Lane” became most renowned. A folk tale suggests the name also echoes “Dream Lane,” reflecting ancient hopes for childbirth, which over time merged phonetically into the current title.

title: [Charter Recommendation] Cingjing & Hualien Two-way Charter One-Day Tour | Departing from Taroko & Hehuan Mountain & Wuling | Hualien City or Cingjing - KKday
description:
Mountain Pass Road with Guardrails

A narrow mountain road curves sharply along a steep hillside, protected by vivid yellow and red guardrails. Light snow covers parts of the grassy slope and roadside, indicating a chilly, high-altitude environment. In the distance, rolling green hills stretch beneath a partly cloudy sky, creating a sense of remoteness and natural beauty.

This image illustrates a segment of the chartered one-day tour route between Cingjing and Hualien, which traverses Taiwan’s highest highways. Travelers on this eight-hour excursion can expect winding roads, snow-dusted peaks, and panoramic views of Taroko Gorge, Hehuan Mountain, and Wuling, all accessible via private or shared vehicles with flexible departure and return options.

title: 阿里山國家森林遊樂區 > 觀光景點 > 交通部觀光署
description:
Alishan Forest Railway Train

A bright red narrow-gauge train winds its way through the dense cedar forests of Taiwan’s Alishan National Forest Recreation Area. The vintage carriages, painted in red and white, stand out against the lush greenery and towering trees. Alongside the tracks, a moss-covered stone wall and wooden railing guide the path, enhancing the historic atmosphere.

Alishan is famed for its forest railway, built during the Japanese colonial era to transport timber. Today, it offers visitors a tranquil ride through ancient woods, misty valleys, and scenic mountain landscapes. The legend of Chief Abali, who first hunted in these forests over 250 years ago, lends cultural depth to this natural wonder.

title: 台南安平｜台南一日遊懶人包！拜訪文青咖啡廳、大啖美食小吃～漫遊古都，欣賞浪漫夕陽-輕旅行
description:
Anping Fort Watchtower

A sturdy red-brick wall with patterned crenellations forms the base of Anping Fort, its weathered surface bearing the marks of centuries. Above the wall, a white-painted watchtower capped with a red-tiled roof peeks out from behind a canopy of lush green trees, offering a striking contrast against the clear blue sky.

Originally built by the Dutch in the 17th century and later reconstructed under Japanese rule, the fort’s current appearance includes a restored lookout tower that visitors can ascend. The surrounding banyan trees and historic masonry evoke the site’s layered past, from colonial stronghold to modern tourist landmark.

title: Tainan Film Studio
description:
Chihkan Tower Pavilion

A two-tiered red brick pavilion rises above a neatly trimmed garden at Chihkan Tower in Tainan, Taiwan. The building’s tiled roofs curve upward at the corners, and a balcony on the upper floor offers visitors panoramic views of the grounds. In front of the pavilion, a row of stone steles rests on the backs of sculpted tortoises, while lush hedges and flowering shrubs add vibrant greenery to the scene.

Chihkan Tower began as the Dutch Fort Provintia in 1653 and later served under Koxinga, the Qing Dynasty, and Japanese rule. Its architecture today combines reinforced concrete with traditional wooden details, preserving the original appearance of the historic site. Designated a national first-grade historic site in 1982, it remains open daily for tourists, accessible by city bus or car.

title: 駁二蓬萊倉庫群-高雄駱駝
description:
Penglai Warehouse Complex at Pier-2 Art Center

The Penglai warehouse complex, known locally as the Kaohsiung Camel, features a row of aged grey brick buildings with pitched roofs lining a spacious brick courtyard. Each warehouse displays weathered facades, peeling paint, and exposed red brick foundations, reflecting their industrial heritage. A large metal rolling door and a pair of trash bins are positioned against the nearest building, while the overcast sky and soft daylight highlight the muted tones of the scene.

Taken on October 26, 2022, in Gushan District, Kaohsiung City, this photograph captures the historic atmosphere of the Pier-2 Art Center’s Penglai warehouses. The site’s address is No. 99, Penglai Road, and the temperature was 26°C under cloudy skies.

title: 『高雄 旗津風景区散策(旗後砲台・旗後灯台・鴨角活海産店) 2010/4/29』高雄(台湾)の旅行記・ブログ by 台湾見聞録さんciteフォートラベル
description:
Cihou Lighthouse at Cijin Scenic Area

A pristine white lighthouse building crowns a series of broad stone steps, flanked by neatly trimmed bushes and a lone flagpole bearing Taiwan’s flag. The cylindrical lantern room, topped with a black dome and encircled by a metal balcony, overlooks the coastal landscape beyond. Overcast skies cast a soft, diffused light across the scene, emphasizing the lighthouse’s clean lines and historic character.

This image captures the Cihou Lighthouse, part of the Cijin Scenic Area in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. Visitors often reach the site by taking the KMRT to Sizihwan Station, walking to Gushan Ferry Pier, and crossing to Cijin Island by ferry. After exploring nearby attractions like Cihou Fort and wandering along the seafood street, travelers pause at the lighthouse to admire its maritime heritage and coastal views.

title: 9 Best Beaches in Kenting Taiwan (2026 Winners)
description:
Kenting Baisha Bay Beach Stroll

A pristine golden beach stretches beneath a clear blue sky, where two visitors walk along the shoreline, their footprints trailing behind them. The water is a vivid turquoise, gently rolling onto the soft sand. In the distance, a verdant tree line marks the edge of the coast, offering a lush backdrop to the sunlit scene.

This photograph captures the serene atmosphere of Kenting Baisha Bay in Taiwan, one of the top-rated beaches for swimming and relaxation. The calm waves and bright sunlight create an inviting setting for beachgoers seeking a peaceful seaside escape. With its fine sand and crystal-clear water, this bay exemplifies the natural beauty that draws travelers to Kenting’s renowned coastline.

title: Explore Hualien’s Stunning Taroko National Park on a Day Tour
description:
Taroko Gorge’s Meandering River

A vivid turquoise river carves its way through steep marble walls, revealing the raw power of the Liwu River over centuries. Pebble-strewn banks contrast with the smooth, striated rock faces, while patches of greenery cling to the cliffs above. High on the left, a narrow walkway and tunnel—part of the Swallow Grotto trail—offer visitors a close-up view of the gorge’s dramatic contours.

This section of Taroko National Park showcases the interplay of water and stone that earned it the nickname “Marble Gorge.” The vibrant blue-green water, shaped by mineral-rich marble, flows steadily through the narrow canyon. Visitors often pause on the cliffside path to photograph the swirling currents and towering rock formations, making this spot one of the park’s most photographed vistas.

title: 清水斷崖 > 花蓮縣 > 交通部觀光署
description:
Qingshui Cliffs, Taiwan

The Qingshui Cliffs soar over 1,000 meters above the Pacific Ocean between Heping and Chongde in Hualien County. Covered in dense green foliage, the sheer rock face meets the vibrant turquoise sea below, where waves crash onto a narrow pebble beach. A winding road and tunnel carved into the cliff hint at the dramatic landscape and provide access for travelers.

Recognized as one of Taiwan’s eight major scenic spots, these coastal cliffs lie within Taroko National Park. Visitors are advised to check park advisories for access updates, especially following seismic activity that can affect trail and road conditions.

title: I Could’ve Sat Here All Day — Qixingtan Beach Is That Peaceful | Trip.com Hualien
description:
Peaceful Qixingtan Beach

A serene expanse of smooth pebbles lines the shore of Qixingtan Beach in Hualien, Taiwan, where gentle waves roll in under a blanket of gray clouds. The muted tones of the sea blend with the overcast sky, evoking a sense of calm and solitude. A cool breeze drifts across the scene, enhancing the refreshing coastal ambiance.

This weekday visit reveals the beach’s reputation as a hidden gem for travelers seeking tranquility. The unique pebble shoreline and soft, rhythmic surf make Qixingtan Beach a peaceful retreat away from crowded tourist spots.

title: Jinchengwu Tree (Takeshi Kaneshiro Tree) - All You SHOULD Know Before Going 2026 (with Reviews)
description:
Takeshi Kaneshiro Tree in Chishang

A solitary bishop tree anchors a quiet stretch of Brown Avenue, surrounded by endless emerald rice fields. Visitors on foot and bicycle gather beneath its wide canopy, capturing photos against the backdrop of mist-draped mountains and a clear blue sky. The tree’s fame stems from a 2013 EVA Airlines commercial featuring actor Takeshi Kaneshiro, which transformed this rural landmark into a must-see attraction.

Cyclists often rent bikes near Chishang train station to explore the scenic trails that lace through Taiwan’s Eastern Rift Valley. The area’s peaceful paddies, framed by mountains to the east and west, offer a tranquil escape. While the tree itself is the main draw, travelers appreciate the broader countryside’s serene beauty and the ease of access along Brown Avenue.

title: Coastal Range > Tourism Administration, Republic of China (Taiwan)
description:
Sanxiantai’s Iconic Eight-Arch Bridge

A sinuous footbridge of eight arches stretches from the rocky Taiwanese shoreline out to a small offshore island, its red railings contrasting with the turquoise sea below. Dark volcanic rocks dot the shallow waters, where gentle waves break along the coast. In the distance, lush green hills rise toward misty mountain peaks under a sky streaked with white clouds.

This aerial perspective captures the unique geography of Sanxiantai, part of Taiwan’s Coastal Range. The bridge provides pedestrian access to the island, inviting visitors to explore tide pools and coastal flora. The vivid hues of the ocean, the rugged shoreline, and the verdant backdrop showcase the region’s dramatic natural scenery.

title: 台9線花東縱谷公路
description:
Ruisui Ranch Dairy Pasture

A herd of Holstein cows relaxes and grazes on a broad, muddy field at Ruisui Ranch in Hualien County’s East Rift Valley. The pasture is framed by lush, forested hills under an overcast sky, reflecting the region’s fertile landscape between the Coastal and Central Mountain Ranges.

Ruisui Ranch encompasses multiple dairy farms across 40 hectares, housing nearly 300 Holstein cows. The area benefits from pristine water sources, fresh air, and abundant grasslands, producing rich and flavorful milk. This pastoral setting is part of the scenic Tai 9 Line green corridor, celebrated for its varied agricultural vistas and natural beauty.
